_comment: Two kinds of bot, and confusing them is the mistake this whole tool exists
to stop. The lists are deliberately conservative: an agent nobody can
confidently classify goes in `unclassified` and is reported as undecided,
because a checker that guesses is the thing it is trying to replace.
Sources are each vendor's own published crawler documentation, read rather
than remembered. Where a vendor runs several agents with different jobs,
each is listed separately — that is precisely where the confusion starts.

training._what: Collects pages to train a model. Refusing it says 'do not train on me'. It is deliberate, common, entirely reasonable, and it does NOT remove you from an assistant's answers.

agents.CCBot: Common Crawl. Not an AI company, but its archive is a common training input.
agents.Google-Extended: Gemini training ONLY. It has no effect on Google Search ranking or inclusion. This is the single most misread token in robots.txt.
agents.Applebot-Extended: Apple Intelligence training opt-out. Plain Applebot still crawls for Siri and Spotlight, so blocking this does not remove you from Apple's answers.
agents.Amazonbot: Amazon; documented as supporting Alexa answers and training. Listed here because its primary documented purpose is collection, not answer-time retrieval.

retrieval._what: Fetches or indexes a page so an assistant or a search engine can READ and CITE it at the moment somebody asks. Refuse these and you genuinely cannot be recommended.

agents.ChatGPT-User: Fetches a page live when a ChatGPT user's question needs it.
agents.OAI-SearchBot: Indexes pages for ChatGPT search results.
agents.Claude-User: Fetches a page live for a Claude user's request.
agents.Perplexity-User: Fetches a page live for a Perplexity user.
agents.Googlebot: Google Search. Blocking this removes you from Google, and from AI Overviews with it.
agents.MistralAI-User: Fetches a page live for a Mistral user.

unclassified._what: Named in the wild, but this file will not assert which job it does. Reported as undecided rather than counted either way.

agents.Bytespider-Search: Documentation is inconsistent about whether this is collection or retrieval.
agents.FacebookBot: Documented for link previews and for language-model work at different times.
agents.PetalBot: Huawei; documented as a search crawler, also reported as a collection agent.
